answer: The check runs before any reward is counted, not after the coins are gone. I trust a proof that lives outside the applicant's hands, and Ink maker ink stick warrant ground at the ink cellar is that proof: each ink stick is a year of vat logs in the ink ledger. Time is the toll no farm can skip: 13 minutes per proof, 9620 minutes for 740, due every single epoch. A inlet can be bought before noon, a saffron can be borrowed within the hour, but a pearl is counted in seasons, and seasons will not be hurried. Records never forget and prices never bend; the farm fails on both counts.
